d.chapter: Economic Geography — Sectors of the Economy
d.notions: Quaternary sector, research, information and communication technology (ICT), knowledge economy.
d.focus: Definition and examples of the quaternary sector.
d.competence: Learners are able to explain how research and digital tools improve daily life and farming, and to use them responsibly.
objectives: Explain the importance of the quaternary sector for development.
recall: The tertiary sector provides services: trade, transport, banking, social services and tourism.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: what a research centre does.
situation: For many years, the maize of farmers near Garoua was destroyed by drought. Then researchers created a new variety of maize that grows quickly and resists drought.
Now farmers harvest much more. Fatimé wonders in which sector these researchers work, since they do not farm, make goods or sell things.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Fatimé does not know in which sector the researchers work.
What did the researchers create, and how did it help farmers?
They created a new maize variety that grows quickly and resists drought, so farmers harvest more.
How can research help other farmers in North Cameroon?
Researchers can create better seeds for sorghum, cotton and rice, and teach farmers new methods.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the quaternary sector, which produces knowledge and information that help all other sectors.

qa.q: Researchers, computer programmers and experts produce knowledge and information. What sector do they belong to?
qa.a: They belong to the quaternary sector.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: The quaternary sector is the sector of the economy based on knowledge, research and information.

qa.q: Give two examples of research centres in Cameroon.
qa.a: IRAD (Institute of Agricultural Research for Development) and the research laboratories of the universities, such as the University of Maroua.

qa.q: How do information and communication technologies (ICT) help farmers and traders?
qa.a: With mobile phones and the internet, they can get market prices, weather forecasts and advice, and they can sell online.

qa.q: Why do rich countries invest a lot of money in the quaternary sector?
qa.a: Because research and technology create new products, improve production and make the economy stronger.

sum.title: II. Examples and Importance
sum.intro: The main quaternary activities and their importance are the following:
items: A. Scientific Research
Researchers create new knowledge, medicines and better seeds, as at IRAD and in universities.
B. Information and Communication Technology
ICT workers create software, websites, mobile applications and manage data.
C. Consulting and Education Planning
Experts give advice to governments and companies, and plan education and training.
D. Importance
The quaternary sector improves all the other sectors: better seeds for farmers, new machines for factories and new services.

evaluation: The quaternary sector is the sector based on knowledge, research and information.
Give two examples of quaternary activities.
Two quaternary activities are scientific research and computer programming.
Classify these jobs into the four sectors: fisherman, baker, taxi driver, researcher.
Fisherman: primary. Baker: secondary. Taxi driver: tertiary. Researcher: quaternary.
remediation: The sector based on knowledge and research is the ______ sector.
The agricultural research institute of Cameroon is ______.
A person who writes computer programs is a ______.
Research helps farmers by creating better ______.
A baker works in the ______ sector.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. quaternary 2. IRAD 3. communication 4. programmer 5. seeds 6. secondary
d.homework: On a map of Africa in your atlas, find Cameroon and name the four oceans and seas that surround Africa.
